Theory Background

ZScoreES on a quadratic landscape f(θ) = −½θTQθ obeys a noisy linear recurrence:

θ_{t+1} = (I − γQ) θ_t + η_t,    γ = ασ/σ_R(θ_t)
E[θ_t]  ≈ (I − γ₀Q)^t θ₀         (frozen-σ_R approximation)

In the eigenbasis of Q (eigenvalues λ𝑖, eigenvectors u𝑖), defining c𝑖(t) = u𝑖Tθ_t:

E[c𝑖(t)] = (1 − γ₀λ𝑖)^t · c𝑖(0)                [D1, D2]
Var[c𝑖(∞)] = (α²/N) / (1 − γ_k²)    [D3 Model 0 — proposition]
Bug found: The original noise floor formula used σ_R frozen at θ=0 (where ‖v‖→0), making γ* too large and inflating Var[c𝑖(∞)] by 3–4×. The Q² anisotropic correction (Model 1 vs Model 0) is negligible. The dynamic-γ model (Model 2) matches empirical variance within ~10%.

D3 — Noise Floor: Three-Model Comparison (Key New Finding)

Result: M0 ≈ M1 (Q² correction negligible). Both overestimate by 3–4×. Model 2 (dynamic γ) matches empirical to ∼10%. Root cause: frozen-γ* uses σ_R at θ=0, which is too small, inflating γ* and shrinking the OU denominator (1−γ_k²).

Interpretation

  • M0 ≈ M1: The Q² anisotropic term 2σ⁴Q²/σ_R² is negligible relative to I_d for σ=0.1. Both models give identical totals to 4 significant figures.
  • 3–4× overestimate in M0/M1: Frozen γ* uses σ_R at θ=0, where σ_R² ≈ ½σ⁴Tr[Q²] — too small. This inflates γ* beyond its trajectory-averaged value, shrinking (1−γ_k²) and blowing up the predicted floor.
  • M2 within ~10%: Using empirical σ_R(t) trajectory fixes the contraction correctly. Remaining gap (~0.3–1.0× per mode) comes from the vvT term in Cov[Δθ] being nonzero mid-trajectory.
  • What the theory needs: Self-consistent σ_R at a characteristic trajectory distance, or analytic dynamic-OU solution with γ(t) = ασ/σ_R(‖θ_t‖).

D1 — Mean Trajectory vs Frozen-σ_R Theory

Theory: E[c𝑖(t)] = (1−γ₀λ𝑖)t c𝑖(0). Frozen-γ underpredicts convergence speed by 3–7×; the mean decays faster than the frozen approximation because γ grows dynamically.

Cluster summary across σ

D4 — ZScoreES vs Gradient Descent (Cluster)

ES (N=30 evals/step) vs exact GD with optimal learning rate. Per step: ES is slower. Per total function evaluations: ES requires ~N× more evaluations for the same convergence. ES advantage: robust to observation noise ξ where GD degrades.

Main implication for theory: The simplified proposition (η ~ N(0, α²/N · I)) has the right noise structure — the Q² anisotropic correction is genuinely negligible here. The stationary variance overestimate comes entirely from using γ* frozen at θ=0. The fix: evaluate σ_R at a characteristic trajectory distance (e.g., time-averaged ‖Qθ_t‖), or derive a self-consistent equation for the stationary variance that accounts for the dynamic relationship σ_R = σ_R(‖θ‖).
